EdgeHub blogging features are powered by the blog plugin. Here are a few tips you might find useful. Simply add Markdown files (or folders) to the blog directory. Regular blog authors can be added to authors.yml. The blog post date can be extracted from filenames, such as: 2019-05-30-welcome.md 2019-05-30-welcome/index.md A blog post folder can be convenient to co-locate blog post images: The blog supports tags as well! And if you don't want a blog: just delete this directory, and use blog: false in your EdgeHub config.
Global management features that are independent of any project — login, licensing, users and system settings. Most are reached through the application bar.

The user authentication page for DataWorX. You are redirected here when there is no session or the session has ended. On first use, log in with the super administrator account admin and the initial password 1234.
On first login you must set an initial password along with the welcome screen. Passwords must be 8 to 15 characters.

After a configured number of failed login attempts, login is blocked for a configured period. When locked, the number of failures and the remaining lock time are displayed. Configure this under System settings → User security.

When a password expiry period is set, logging in after the period has passed shows the password change screen. Clicking Change later keeps the password and resets the expiry period. Configure this under Member management.

Edit the information of the logged-in user. User name — 3 to 30 characters, English or Korean The ID and role cannot be changed. Click the Set password button at the bottom right of the profile card to change the password. It takes effect immediately when you confirm the modal.

:::info Administrator only The license page can only be used with administrator privileges. ::: If no license is registered, a Trial license allowing 1,000 tags for 14 days from the DataWorX installation date is granted automatically. After 14 days a license must be registered.
A license key is provided by e-mail when DataWorX is purchased. EID — The login ID for offline license registration Product Key — The product number for online license registration

Use this in an environment with internet access. Click the Edit button at the top right of License Management. Select Online as the registration method. Enter the Product Key from the license e-mail into Product Key (pkId) and save. Confirm the registration on the license information screen.

Use this in an environment without internet access. Click the Download offline key button at the top left of the License Management table to download DataWorX_Information.c2v. From a PC with internet access, go to ls-electric.prod.sentinelcloud.com/customer. Log in with the EID or Product ID listed in the license file. Click Activate Offline and enter the e-mail address that should receive the license activation file. Click Select File and upload the *.c2v file saved in step 1. Click Complete Activation to activate the offline license. An Activation was successful message appears; download the offline license file (.V2CP). A compressed copy is also sent to the e-mail address you entered. Upload the downloaded .V2CP file and click Save. Confirm the registration on the license information screen.

Moves a license in use to another PC. Executable path: [DataWorX installation path]\ETC\LicenseRehostTool\LicenseRehostTool.exe With the default installation: C:\EdgeHub\DataWorX\ETC\LicenseRehostTool\LicenseRehostTool.exe note This transfer method applies from DataWorX v4.0.0 onward. If you need to migrate or keep license keys from a version earlier than v4.0.0, contact LS ELECTRIC. Two PCs are involved — the New PC and the Current PC. Run LicenseRehostTool.exe on both. 1. [New PC] Create the info file (.id)​ Run LicenseRehostTool.exe on the new PC. Go to the Step 1. Generate New PC Info (New PC) area. Click the ... button next to Save PC Info File (.id) and choose a save path. Click Create at the bottom right to generate the info file (.id). Copy the .id file to the current PC using a USB drive or similar. 2. [Current PC] Create the transfer file (.h2h)​ Run LicenseRehostTool.exe on the current PC. Go to the Step 2. Export License File (Current PC) area. Select the product license to transfer from the Select License to Transfer list. Click the ... button next to Import New PC Info File (.id) and load the .id file from step 1. Click the ... button next to Save Transfer File and choose where the transfer file (.h2h) is saved. Click Create to generate the transfer file (.h2h) and copy it back to the new PC. 3. [New PC] Activate the license​ On the new PC, run the product application and register the .h2h file from step 2 in the license registration window to complete activation. :::danger Essential precautions 1. Check for running product sessions — Before creating the .h2h file on the current PC, the product application must be completely closed. If a session remains after closing, open http://localhost:1947/_int_/sessions.html and click Disconnect in the Actions column for that product session. 2. Do not lose the transfer file (.h2h) — If the generated .h2h file is lost, it cannot be regenerated under any circumstances. The license then becomes unusable on both the current and the new PC. License loss caused by failing to back up in advance is not covered by free reissue or compensation. :::

Alarms are a critical part of DataWorX and any SCADA system. This document describes how DataWorX processes alarms and how alarm groups are configured. info In DataWorX an alarm can only be set when the tag type is Analog or Digital, and alarms are only processed when the tag value was collected successfully.

Tag type Alarm category Alarm type Occurrence rule Recovery rule Analog Boundary HH Alarm Tag value is greater than or equal to HH After an HH alarm, cleared when the tag value falls below HH HI Alarm Tag value is HI or greater but less than HH After an HI alarm, cleared when the tag value is below HI or reaches HH LO Alarm Tag value is LO or less but greater than LL After a LO alarm, cleared when the tag value is above LO or reaches LL LL Alarm Tag value is LL or less After an LL alarm, cleared when the tag value rises above LL Variance Variance alarm The tag value deviates from the previous value by at least the baseline value After a variance alarm, cleared when the deviation falls below the baseline value Separation Major separation alarm The tag value differs from the reference value by at least the major separation value After a major separation alarm, cleared when the difference falls below the major separation value Secondary separation alarm The tag value differs from the reference value by at least the secondary separation value and less than the major separation value Cleared when the difference reaches the major separation value or falls below the secondary separation value Digital Digital ON The tag value is ON Cleared when the tag value is OFF OFF The tag value is OFF Cleared when the tag value is ON ON → OFF The tag value changes from ON to OFF Cleared as soon as it occurs OFF → ON The tag value changes from OFF to ON Cleared as soon as it occurs Change The tag value changes Cleared as soon as it occurs

The most commonly used alarm when the tag type is Analog. Four boundary values are configured: HH, HI, LO, LL. The value range is divided horizontally, so the corresponding alarm is triggered when the tag value enters a zone and cleared when it leaves. Each boundary can have a deadband area. When an alarm deadband value is set, the deadband rule is applied based on the direction of change and the zone the value is in.

Triggered when the tag's current value changes from its previous value by at least the variance value set in the tag properties. Once triggered, it is cleared when subsequent changes fall below the configured variance value. Use it when a tag value should not change significantly. Variance alarms are not subject to the deadband rule.

Triggered by the difference between the major and secondary separation of a tag value relative to a reference value. Separation alarms follow the same deadband rules as boundary alarms. Differences from boundary alarms: Separation alarms have no upper and lower division. The reference value can be an absolute value or a relative value (another tag's value).

When the tag type is Digital, alarms are configured based on the previous and current value. Alarm type Description ON Triggered when the value is ON, cleared when it is OFF OFF Triggered when the value is OFF, cleared when it is ON ON → OFF Triggered when the value changes from ON to OFF and cleared at the same time OFF → ON Triggered when the value changes from OFF to ON and cleared at the same time Change Triggered when the value changes and cleared at the same time

Alarm delay means that when a field value shows an anomaly, the alarm is not raised immediately. Instead, the value after the configured delay is compared with the value before the first trigger, and the alarm is raised from that.

Two items must be set. 1. Set the delay time Enter the delay time under Tag → Alarm settings. This value is set per tag and applies to all alarms for that tag. 2. Set the alarm delay flag Open [project path]/[project name]/Config/ehDataProcess.ini and set: DP_ALARMDELAY_FLAG=1 Start the DataWorX runtime to apply the alarm delay time. warning Setting an alarm delay time can put a significant load on the DataWorX runtime and should only be used when strictly necessary.

Alarm groups divide tags into logical sets so that bulk actions can be taken per management point. Raised alarms can be filtered by alarm group when querying, or handled in LogicFlow. Property Description Alarm group name Required. The name of the alarm group Alarm group description Description of the alarm group Level The level of the alarm group (1–10). When a tag has no alarm level of its own, the alarm group's level is used Add, info, edit and delete are performed through the sub navigation menu, the table row more menu, and the buttons at the top right of the table.

DataWorX lets you change the web access port used by the browser and the server (backend) port that the web server (nginx) forwards requests to. Configuration file path: [DataWorX installation path]\bin\EngineeringTool\Client\conf With the default installation: C:\EdgeHub\DataWorX\bin\EngineeringTool\Client\conf Configuration file Purpose Default client-port.conf Web access port used by the browser 7600 server-port.conf Port used by the DataWorX server (backend) 5000 Browser requests arrive at the web access port and are forwarded internally to the server port.
Open client-port.conf in a text editor and change the listen value. listen 7600; For example, to use port 8080, change it to listen 8080; and connect via http://[server IP]:8080.

Open server-port.conf and change the port in the proxy_pass address. proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:5000; The DataWorX server runs on the port set in this file, and the web server forwards requests to the same port. If the port value cannot be found, the default of 5000 is used. :::caution Notes on changing ports After changing the configuration files you must restart the DataWorX services (server and web server) for the change to take effect. Avoid ports already in use by other programs. A port conflict prevents normal startup. The new port must be allowed in the Windows Firewall for external access. :::

LogicFlow is one of the components of DataWorX. You compose flows from a wide range of nodes and use event-based modelling to implement data lookup, processing and input quickly. Applications built this way can be edited and deployed while the runtime is running. LogicFlow runs on the Node.js runtime, and the editor works in any HTML5-capable browser. :::info Prerequisites Engineering LogicFlow (built on Node-RED) requires a working knowledge of JavaScript and SQL. Using additional libraries or custom nodes also requires understanding the structure and behaviour of those libraries. :::
Provides a wide range of built-in nodes, with the option to install more. The DataWorX tag interface is available. Real-time LogicFlow data can be exported to an external DB.

Dedicated nodes for DataWorX integration. Node Description tag value Reads DataWorX tag values into the flow whenever input arrives. A node that runs JavaScript code against the incoming msg, with access to the DataWorX tag interface from within the script. Node properties: Name — The name shown in the flow editor Code — The JavaScript code executed at runtime Outputs — The number of node outputs. Sending msg as an array delivers each element to its own output Function groups provided: Tag functions — such as getTagVal Project functions History data query functions Realtime alarm functions Global tag value reference Event logging functions getTagVal fetches DataWorX real-time tag values immediately and can be called in several forms. // By tag name getTagVal("D10.BLUE_01.ENCODER_TEMP_AXIS_1", function (value) { msg.payload = value; node.send(msg); }); // By array of tag names getTagVal( ["D10.BLUE_01.ENCODER_TEMP_AXIS_2", "D10.BLUE_01.ENCODER_TEMP_AXIS_3"], function (value) { msg.payload = value; node.send(msg); } ); // By tag group name getTagVal("D10.BLUE_01", function (value) { msg.payload = value; node.send(msg); });

inject · debug · complete · catch · status · link in · link out · comment The inject node starts a flow by sending a message manually or at a set interval. The payload can be a string, the current time, a JavaScript object and more, and the repeat setting offers "at a set interval", "at a set interval within a time range" and "at a specific time".
function · switch · change · range · template · delay · trigger · exec · filter The API reference covers the node, context, flow, global, RED and env objects, plus other modules and functions.
mqtt in · mqtt out · http in · http response · http request · websocket in · websocket out · tcp in · tcp out · tcp request · udp in · udp out

Node Description split Splits a message into a message sequence. Strings/buffers split on a delimiter, arrays by size, and objects into key/value pairs. The msg.parts property records the relationship to the original message join Combines a message sequence into a single message, with three modes including automatic sort Sorts a message sequence batch Groups messages into batches

Node Description csv Two-way conversion between CSV strings and JavaScript objects. Configure column names, the separator (comma by default) and the output payload format html HTML parsing json JSON ↔ object conversion xml XML ↔ object conversion yaml YAML ↔ object conversion

Choose append, overwrite or delete, with encoding and automatic directory creation options read file Reads file contents as a string or a binary buffer watch Watches files and directories for changes mysql MySQL integration :::tip Specifying filenames Specifying the filename as an absolute path is recommended. The msg.filename property can also be used, but then the file is closed after every operation, which can degrade performance. :::

DataWorX is a web-based software that bridges the OT and IT domains. It runs on Microsoft Windows and provides broad extensibility, high reliability, fast processing and operational convenience. With DataWorX you can collect, process and store data from a wide range of equipment in the OT domain, apply field-specific logic through programming, and build a system that reliably and flexibly delivers data to upper-level systems in the IT domain. :::info Document version This document is written against DataWorX v4.1.0 (online manual v3.0.6). :::
An open structure built on open source, with excellent extensibility and compatibility, enables reliable communication with devices and effective interfacing with other systems.
Create and manage different types of projects, and use the copy feature for easy engineering.

Two perspectives on tag management provide engineering efficiency and operator convenience at the same time. Feature Description Physical View A tree-style tag navigator that follows the equipment layout. Device configuration and tag work can be done together Logical View Displays logical tag groups like Windows Explorer, so tags can be managed by purpose from an operator's point of view Excel Import/Export Add, output and edit tags in bulk using .xlsx files Operation The value of a memory tag can be a numeric or a logical expression Spreadsheet Add or edit the data of multiple tags at once in a spreadsheet Import LS PLC Import a variable file (CSV) saved from XG5000 and register it automatically as DataWorX tags

Tag Simulator — Run your application exactly as in the field even without a real device, or before communication is established, by feeding tags with data from various rules. This dramatically reduces debugging time. Validate Tags — Check whether the I/O addresses and communication block settings of XGI/XGK series devices are configured correctly, catching misconfigurations before actual communication.

JavaScript-based programming is supported. Instead of writing scripting languages by hand, DataWorX provides a visual development tool called LogicFlow, where field logic is built with a drag-and-drop GUI.

Use a web browser to access the DataWorX system for engineering and runtime. There is no need to be physically present at the DataWorX server machine — everything can be done remotely over the network.

Category Recommended Specification Operating System Windows 11 64-bit Pro or later CPU Intel Core i5 or higher, or equivalent RAM At least 16 GB Storage At least 10 GB of available space Display Graphics card and monitor supporting a minimum resolution of 1024 × 768 Network Ethernet 100 Mbps or higher Communication Port Standard serial port (required when using serial communication) caution Actual performance varies with project size, number of tags, communication cycle, number of connected devices and operating environment. A large number of tags requires higher CPU and RAM specifications.
DataWorX uses an SW license key — a license with no physical copy.

If a project exceeds the number of tags allowed by the SW license, tags are no longer saved and the runtime cannot run. If the license expires, you are returned to the project list screen and can no longer OPEN or RUN a project. Register a new license to continue. Usage examples With a 1,000-tag license, the runtime will not run once you exceed 1,000 tags. With a term license, the runtime runs as long as the registered tag count stays at or below the licensed number during the term. Without a license, the runtime runs with 1,000 tags for 14 days from the date of DataWorX installation. For license registration and transfer procedures, see Administration.

EdgeHub reports query the logging data defined in historian models and generate or print Excel files at a scheduled time. Reports in the product's own format can be generated and printed even where Excel is not installed. Alarm logging data can be queried and printed as a report in the product's own format. Current tag values and tag properties can be queried and produced as Excel or native-format reports. Reports can be printed at the desired time on a variety of cycles: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, free and periodic.

The report duplication feature makes it convenient to create similar types of reports. Reports are organized into Excel Reports, which use an Excel file as a form, and General Reports, which use their own form. Excel reports keep Excel's graphs, charts, formatting and statistics. The General Report form editor makes table-based report forms easy to build, including tag/alarm/event logging report forms. Results can be produced in PDF, DOC, XLS and TEXT formats.

documents.t: On startup the report runtime reads the report list, checks generation times, and when a generation time arrives it queries the historical data using the report configuration and layout, then writes, saves and prints the report. Selecting [Automatically update output information] in the report editor reflects changes while online. The automatic generation process is recorded in the log at the bottom of the report runtime. Reports are also generated in the PDF/XLS/DOC/TXT formats specified in the report properties.

Key data that needs logging is managed through historian models created for each purpose. At runtime the history engine collects and stores data based on these models. A single tag can be assigned to multiple historian models, enabling varied data analysis. Querying collected data — Available in trends, reports and list trends, with an API for querying from scripts. Automatically calculated statistics and accumulation — Statistical and accumulated data are generated without any separate script or application. Open source database — Uses PostgreSQL, an open-source object-relational database. :::caution Stored time format Timestamps for tags configured in the Tag Historian are stored in the database in UTC. Keep this in mind when querying the database directly. :::

Historian model Description Data available Period Collects tag values every period Analog (current value), Digital (current state) Statistics Generates statistical data for the configured tag every cycle Analog (current value, minimum value, minimum time, maximum value, maximum time, average value, variance), Digital (number of runs, uptime, number of changes) Accumulation Generates statistical data about accumulated values for tags that accumulate Analog (amount of change, current value) String Collects string tag values every interval String (current value)

The minimum collection interval is 1 second, used for fast real-time data logging and mainly for instantaneous value lookups in trends and reports. At runtime it collects and stores on time. With a 2-second interval, logging data is saved at every 0, 2, 4 seconds and so on. Unit Selectable period Seconds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30 Minutes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30 Hours 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 Days 1

The minimum collection period is 1 minute, automatically calculating and storing various statistics. It is used to understand data over a period of time, mainly for statistical queries in reports and trends. At runtime it collects and computes every minute. With a 5-minute interval, if it is currently 2 minutes 20 seconds, the data from 2:20 to 3:00 is computed and stored internally first, then computed internally at 4:00 and 5:00 and updated on time. After the 5-minute mark it starts accumulating new data. Analog — Current value, minimum value, minimum time, maximum value, maximum time, average value Digital — Number of runs, uptime, number of changes Unit Selectable period Minutes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30 Hours 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 Days 1 – 31 Month 1 – 12

Register tags with accumulating characteristics such as watt-hour meters and flow meters to compute and store the amount of change over a period. Hourly, daily and monthly usage can be queried without a separate script or memory tag. At runtime it collects and computes every minute, and automatically generates 1-hour, 1-day and 1-month accumulated data. As a result, the most recent accumulated value is available no matter when you query between model cycles. note Only analog tags can be set for the accumulation model, and it collects every minute without selecting a collection interval or unit. Analog — Amount of change, current value
The minimum collection interval is 1 second, and at runtime it collects and stores on time. The selectable periods are the same as for Period. String — Current value

Tags are the fundamental unit of the DataWorX system. Every feature DataWorX supports operates on registered tags. Tags are divided into the I/O class, which receives signals from field equipment, and the Memory class, which is registered virtually for use by upper-level systems. The property panel shows tag information at a glance and makes tag engineering straightforward. Excel file import/export lets you register and manage large volumes of tag data quickly.
Change the view using the tabs in the sub navigation.

Shows tags according to how they are physically connected to devices, regardless of their names. It is divided by class into I/O and Memory. I/O tags — Tags whose data is collected through communication with actual field devices Memory tags — Tags other than I/O tags, created virtually to make use of data Normal tags — Created directly by the user through engineering Group tags — A logical structure for grouping tags hierarchically, working like folders in a file explorer

Shows tags grouped into a logical hierarchy. The tag name is split on . to build the tree. For a tag named A.B.C, groups A and A.B are created, with the tag A.B.C beneath them. tip The Logical View lets you group plant lines, products or characteristics to manage tags easily.

Rules for converting raw data collected from the device into tag data. Transform rule Description None The raw value is applied as the tag value with no conversion Ratio-Bias Slope/intercept method. Tag value = (Ratio × Raw value) + Bias Ratio Converts by ratio using the min/max of the raw value and the tag value Ratio/Offset Uses the min/max of the raw value and the tag value, then adds an offset Ratio — The value to multiply the raw value by Bias — The value added after multiplying by Ratio Offset — The value added to the result of the ratio conversion

Checks whether the communication addresses and communication blocks of the I/O tags registered on a device are configured correctly. It inspects address format, usable area and bit type, plus the existence, range and enabled state of the containing block, so misconfigurations are caught before actual communication. :::warning Supported drivers The I/O tag validator supports XGI/XGK series drivers only (XGIEnet, XGICnet, XGILoader, XGKEnet, XGKCnet, XGKLoader). ::: Run it from the more menu at the top right of the table via Validate Tags. Select devices — Devices with unsupported drivers are shown greyed out. Select individually or all at once, then click Start validation. Validation results — A summary of total / error / warning / normal counts is shown with the affected tags. The result table has Severity, Tag name, Message, Channel, Device and Address columns. The download button saves io_tag_validation_result_[date]_[time].xlsx. Severity Severity Description Error A configuration error that prevents normal communication. Must be fixed Warning Communication is possible but needs checking (disabled device/block, exceeding the allowed range, etc.) OK No issues found (only tags with issues appear in the result table) Error checks The address contains leading or trailing whitespace An XGI address does not start with %, or an XGK address starts with % The address format cannot be parsed An area unusable by the driver is used The address is a bit address but the tag type is not Digital No block can exist for that area, so no matching block is possible There is no matching communication block, no block for that area, or the address is outside the block range Warning checks The tag belongs to a device that is disabled Auto Block is configured on the device The matching block is disabled The address is outside the allowed range for the area Devices that cannot be found, use an unsupported driver, or fail during validation are reported as errors at the device level rather than per tag.

VisualWorX is a web-based software that performs the role of SCADA, visualizing and displaying data collected in the OT domain. It is based on Microsoft Windows and can be used on Windows 7 SP1, Windows 8.1 Update1, Windows 10 and Windows Server 2012/2022, where .NET Framework 4.6.2 can be installed. With VisualWorX you can configure various graphic objects, charts and event scripts to build monitoring screens that watch and control field conditions. :::info Document version This document is written against VisualWorX v5.0.0 (online manual v3.0.1). :::

VisualWorX uses a client/server structure. On the server side, VisualWorX Server, Runtime and Editor are installed. VisualWorX Runtime and Editor can also be accessed from a web browser. Screens created with the Editor are served through the Server to the Runtime. You can connect to the Server remotely to compose screens and monitor and control field conditions. [VisualWorX Editor] ──compose──▶ [VisualWorX Server] ──serve──▶ [VisualWorX Runtime] ▲ │ tag data [EdgeHub DataWorX]
Various visualization designs are possible using basic shapes such as lines, ovals and rectangles together with control boxes, and animation effects allow more dynamic monitoring designs.
Provides a range of charts for line, bar, scatter, area, pie, donut, bubble, gauge, box plot and normal distribution visualization. See VX Charts for details.

When an event occurs on a monitoring page — a click, a value change, mouse movement and so on — JavaScript can control the screen or change data values to implement detailed behaviour. See Event Script for details.
Use a web browser to access the VisualWorX system for engineering and runtime. There is no need to be at the VisualWorX server machine — all work can be done remotely over the network.

VisualWorX Runtime consists of HTML5 web pages and JavaScript. It receives project information served by VisualWorX Server and performs monitoring. :::caution Prerequisites For VisualWorX Runtime to run correctly, EdgeHub DataWorX and VisualWorX Server must be running. It runs in any browser supporting the HTML5 standard (Chrome, Firefox and others); the latest version of Chrome is recommended. :::

Checking auto login before logging in means that re-entering the Runtime path logs you in automatically and shows the screen you last viewed. Auto login survives the browser being closed and reopened and the server being rebooted. However, it is released 365 days after the login where auto login was enabled. After that, closing and reopening the browser or rebooting the server requires logging in again. Selecting Logout at the top right of the web client toolbar releases auto login and redirects to the login window.

Line redundancy adds a secondary IP so that both are served. Checking line redundancy enables the primary and secondary IP fields. Also checking system redundancy enables six fields: Master IP1/IP2 and Standby IP1/IP2. Enter the IP addresses this server will serve in the primary and secondary IP fields. Enter the primary and secondary IPs served by the Master and Standby sides in Master IP1/IP2 and Standby IP1/IP2. Switching by client connection IP: Connecting on the primary IP → switches to Master IP1 or Standby IP1 according to the system redundancy role Connecting on the secondary IP → switches to Master IP2 or Standby IP2 according to the system redundancy role Example Master PC A serves 10.13.110.110 and 10.13.111.111; Standby PC B serves 10.13.112.112 and 10.13.113.113: PC A — primary/secondary IP and Master IP1/IP2 = 10.13.110.110, 10.13.111.111; Standby IP1/IP2 = 10.13.112.112, 10.13.113.113 PC B — primary/secondary IP and Standby IP1/IP2 = 10.13.112.112, 10.13.113.113; Master IP1/IP2 = 10.13.110.110, 10.13.111.111

System redundancy places a Master and Standby IP so that clients switch to the other side when one goes down. Checking system redundancy enables the primary IP, Master IP1 and Standby IP1 fields. Example PC A (10.13.110.110) is Master and PC B (10.13.111.111) is Standby: PC A primary IP → 10.13.110.110 / PC B primary IP → 10.13.111.111 On both PCs, Master IP1 = 10.13.110.110 and Standby IP1 = 10.13.111.111 :::warning IP rules For the Master role: primary IP = Master IP1, secondary IP = Master IP2 For the Standby role: primary IP = Standby IP1, secondary IP = Standby IP2 The Master IP and Standby IP must differ from each other :::

Client redundancy switches the screen automatically when a client connects and system redundancy is configured. When both Master and Standby PCs are active, connecting to the Standby PC switches to the Master PC screen. If the Master PC shuts down while its screen is open, the screen switches automatically to the Standby PC. When the Master PC recovers, the Standby PC screen switches back to the Master PC screen automatically. note Connecting with localhost or 127.0.0.1 is treated as engineering and does not switch screens. To avoid automatic client switching when connecting to the Master or Standby PC, uncheck client auto-switching on the login screen before logging in. After logging in you can re-enable it from the toolbar in the runtime top menu.

Install OpenSSL from Win32/Win64 OpenSSL. Run the installed file to open a command prompt. Create a certs folder in your user account. Files generated by OpenSSL are created under this folder. Enter the following commands in order. openssl genrsa -out privKey.pem 1024 openssl req -new -key privKey.pem -out private-csr.pem openssl x509 -req -days 730 -in private-csr.pem -signkey privKey.pem -out cert.pem caution Enter the PC's IP address or localhost for the Common Name. Three files are created in the SSL path after the commands complete.

Run Service Settings → Secure communication → Manage certificates. Click Register in certificate management. Register cert.pem as the certificate file and privKey.pem as the private key file. Connect to https://(the configured address) to see the VisualWorX screen.

If you need to migrate or keep license keys from a version earlier than v5.0.0, contact LS ELECTRIC. Two PCs are involved — the New PC and the Current PC. Run LicenseRehostTool.exe on both. 1. [New PC] Create the info file (.id) Run LicenseRehostTool.exe on the new PC. Go to the Step 1. Generate New PC Info (New PC) area. Click the ... button next to Save PC Info File (.id) and choose a save path. Click Create to generate the info file (.id) and copy it to the current PC. 2. [Current PC] Create the transfer file (.h2h) Run LicenseRehostTool.exe on the current PC. Go to the Step 2. Export License File (Current PC) area. Select the product license to transfer from the Select License to Transfer list. Click the ... button next to Import New PC Info File (.id) and load the .id file from step 1. Click the ... button next to Save Transfer File and choose a save path. Click Create to generate the transfer file (.h2h) and copy it back to the new PC. 3. [New PC] Activate the license On the new PC, run the product application and register the .h2h file from step 2 in the license registration window to complete activation. :::danger Essential precautions 1. Check for running product sessions — Before creating the .h2h file on the current PC, the product application must be completely closed. If a session remains after closing, open http://localhost:1947/_int_/sessions.html and click Disconnect in the Actions column for that product session. 2. Do not lose the transfer file (.h2h) — If the generated .h2h file is lost, it cannot be regenerated under any circumstances. The license then becomes unusable on both the current and the new PC. License loss caused by failing to back up in advance is not covered by free reissue or compensation. :::
